{"id":"APL-36","uuid":"06880622-b48b-4010-8c85-6c01e7911024","title":"[SAHA-013] Caseload assignment and transfer","description":"## User / outcome

As an authorised assignment administrator, I want effective-dated caseload transfers that preserve open work and receiving-team acknowledgement, so responsibility remains clear when a worker's assignment changes.

**Scope boundary:** Restrict former access and prevent duplicate ownership or orphaned urgent tasks. A transfer does not establish new urgency rules.

## Canonical scope and hierarchy

Scope ID: SAHA-013; type: functional. Original IDs: BR-ID-04.
CWO references: CWO-031. Decision references: DEC-04.
Primary epic: WP01; related work packages: WP01. Source original release(s): R1.
This is one of the 160 reconciled scope items. 1 original requirement(s) map here exactly once.

## Original requirement and acceptance text

### BR-ID-04 — Caseload assignment and transfer

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Households, patients and tasks shall have effective assignment dates and responsible teams. Transfer shall preserve open work, restrict former access and identify unresolved responsibility gaps.

Acceptance: Transferring a worker's caseload moves eligible open tasks, records acknowledgement and prevents duplicate ownership or orphaned urgent tasks.

## Additional CWO acceptance / refusal criteria

No additional CWO criterion assigned to this owner; original criteria are retained unchanged.

## Original test scenarios — not executed acceptance

### TC-BR-ID-04-A — Caseload assignment and transfer acceptance

Type: Functional; source role: QA with Deployment administrator and identity steward; fixture: FX-ID-04.
Preconditions: Synthetic tenant A; verified actor with intended scope; relevant pack and connector test profile active; reset fixture before execution.
Steps: 1. Load FX-ID-04. 2. Assignment changes carry effective dates and an explicit list of transferred open tasks with receiving ownership. 3. Capture UI/API results and stored receipt or audit evidence.
Expected: Transferring a worker's caseload moves eligible open tasks, records acknowledgement and prevents duplicate ownership or orphaned urgent tasks.
Formal status: Not run; no engineering subset automatically passes this case.

### TC-BR-ID-04-B — Caseload assignment and transfer adverse condition

Type: Negative or recovery; source role: QA with Deployment administrator and identity steward; fixture: FX-ID-04-NEG.
Preconditions: Isolated synthetic tenant; begin from the corresponding acceptance scenario; inject only the named adverse condition.
Steps: 1. Establish the normal precondition. 2. Transfer a caseload with an unresolved urgent task; the task cannot become unassigned. 3. Inspect user state, side effects, audit and any recovery queue.
Expected: Transfer a caseload with an unresolved urgent task; the task cannot become unassigned. Evidence must show the actual final state and any accountable unresolved work.
Formal status: Not run; no engineering subset automatically passes this case.

## Authorization, error and recovery contract

Current server role/tenant/assignment/purpose, audit and version constraints remain applicable. Before execution, freeze authorised positive behaviour, out-of-scope/changed-authority refusal, invalid input, unavailable dependency, stale version and uncertain-save recovery wherever relevant. Inspect actual code/API/data and inherited failures; preserve targets and no-side-effect guarantees. Do not substitute an assumed UI or reference API catalogue for a current implementation contract.

## Current evidence and readiness

BR-ID-04: source assessment "partial"; target checkpoint R14. Full remaining scope stays open; see authoritative requirements/assessment.tsv and current evidence-map. Remaining: A timed trigger that has actually run on the hosted Worker (the job needs the Workers Paid plan and has not been seen firing on Cloudflare; on a host with no trigger the application time depends on use), locality transfer, field acceptance of handovers and approved urgency rules.
Canonical item remains Backlog/unqualified. Current local source/assessment may contain bounded implemented components; original formal acceptance is not thereby passed. No named executor, estimate or delivery date is invented.
Not part of the first D01–D08 implementation tasks; later prioritisation requires sponsor decision and dependency checks.

## Technical work and delivery

Requirement-linked engineering subtasks retain ENG IDs, source outcomes, owner roles, dependencies and tests. Inspect current reuse and freeze a minimal ready slice before coding; no bulk implementation dispatch. GitHub #188 remains the single delivery controller. Isolated qualified story PRs, final-code CI/review/native approvals and exact hosting/smoke evidence govern delivery.
No real patient/recipient, provider activation, paid services, new hosting, parallel database, clinical policy or destructive migration is authorised by this backlog.

Sources: [scope row](<https://github.com/nakul175/saha-health/blob/9e74b6a4648aa0a0a9e3fa32474cb4c943f1aea1/docs/current/community-worker-os/scope.tsv>), [additional criteria](<https://github.com/nakul175/saha-health/blob/9e74b6a4648aa0a0a9e3fa32474cb4c943f1aea1/docs/current/community-worker-os/new-criteria.tsv>), [source BRD requirements](<https://github.com/nakul175/saha-health/blob/7668a03d97c1ae62174f09e65ccd5a5717120be6/requirements/brd-v1.1.json>), [formal catalogue](<https://github.com/nakul175/saha-health/blob/7668a03d97c1ae62174f09e65ccd5a5717120be6/docs/reference/workbook/Test-Catalogue.csv>), [delivery gates](<https://linear.app/aplyd-sandbox/document/saha-story-readiness-and-delivery-gates-3fbcfc7ee2e7>).

## v4.2 planning refinement — source preserved

Author recommendation for planning only. Original requirements, frozen criteria, native status/priority/milestone/assignee and historic evidence remain unchanged. Do not weaken criteria to obtain a pass.

### Priority, sequence and forecast

Retain original Must-before-Should/Could and source-release ordering; use risk reduction and prerequisites to choose one bounded slice before adding further product surface.

Source priorities: Must; release: R1. Source package inputs: none recorded. These are inspection inputs, not whole-epic completion requirements.

Recommended size: 2–5 engineering effort days, low confidence. Method: owned requirement count plus interface/device/source-gap uncertainty; inspect current reuse first. Excludes approval/partner wait, participant recruitment and observation windows; no staffing/date commitment.

### Scenario coverage and evidence contract

* Positive: Run TC-BR-ID-04-A using the source-named fixture, actor, preconditions and exact Expected oracle; cover effective-dated caseload transfers that preserve open work and receiving-team acknowledgement.
* Refusal/adverse: Run TC-BR-ID-04-B; retained source adverse/recovery case: Transfer a caseload with an unresolved urgent task; the task cannot become unassigned.. Its source label does not by itself establish refusal coverage.
* Error/recovery refinement: Fail a caseload-transfer acknowledgement with an open urgent task. Keep a visible accountable queue and both effective assignment states; do not duplicate ownership or silently orphan work.
* Authorization refinement: For authorised assignment administrator performing “effective-dated caseload transfers that preserve open work and receiving-team acknowledgement”: Use a revoked/wrong-tenant or no-longer-assigned identity and a guessed object ID; current server role, tenant, assignment, delegation and purpose must deny the protected read/action before content or side effects.

Bind source/configuration and synthetic fixture version to actual UI/API/state/side-effect/audit outputs; record every failed, skipped and untested case separately. Planned scenarios remain Not run, and local reuse evidence cannot satisfy full formal or live/domain approval.

### Shared gates and remaining decisions

Link [SAHA-READY-1.0 and SAHA-DONE-1.0](<https://linear.app/aplyd-sandbox/document/saha-story-readiness-and-delivery-gates-3fbcfc7ee2e7>); apply the engineering/synthetic scope and exact version, alongside this issue’s unchanged source acceptance. Shared checklist completeness cannot approve domain decisions or stand in for observed delivery.
